gloss: A piece of work or a document handed in for consideration.
examples: The journal received four hundred *submissions*.
Your *submission* must be in by Friday.
Late *submissions* will not be read.

gloss: A smaller part of a section of a document or law.
examples: See *subsection* B of the contract.
The chapter is broken into four *subsections*.
That rule is buried in a *subsection*.

gloss: A smaller group that is part of a larger one.
examples: Only a small *subset* of users saw the error.
We tested a *subset* of the samples.
The data was split into two *subsets*.

gloss: The minimum food and money needed to stay alive.
examples: Many families live at *subsistence* level.
They practice *subsistence* farming.
The wage is barely above *subsistence*.

gloss: A group within a species whose members differ slightly from the rest.
examples: This *subspecies* lives only on one island.
Biologists recognize three *subspecies* of the bird.
The northern *subspecies* is larger.
contrast: The plural is spelled and said the same as the singular.

gloss: The use of tricks or deception to reach a goal.
examples: He got the documents by *subterfuge*.
The whole deal was arranged through *subterfuge*.
No *subterfuge* was needed — they simply asked.

gloss: The quality of being delicate, understated, and not obvious.
examples: His acting has real *subtlety*.
The sauce lacks *subtlety*.
There's no *subtlety* in their advertising.

gloss: The act of taking one number away from another.
examples: Second graders are learning *subtraction*.
She's fast at addition but slow at *subtraction*.
Check your *subtraction* on the last line.

gloss: The suburbs and the way of life found there.
examples: He grew up in the heart of *suburbia*.
The movie pokes fun at *suburbia*.
*Suburbia* looks the same from coast to coast.

gloss: Secret action meant to weaken a government or an established system.
examples: He was charged with *subversion*.
The pamphlets were treated as *subversion*.
The film is a quiet *subversion* of the whole genre.

gloss: A speaker built to reproduce the lowest sounds.
examples: The *subwoofer* rattled the windows.
He put a *subwoofer* in the trunk.
Two *subwoofers* sit under the screen.

gloss: The following of one thing after another, or the passing of a position to the next person.
examples: She won three titles in *succession*.
The board has no plan for *succession*.
Rain fell for five days in *succession*.

gloss: Someone who is easily tricked or cheated.
examples: Don't be a *sucker* — read the fine print.
The scam targets *suckers* who want easy money.
I'm a *sucker* for old movies.
